pointers.sentence: Running tasks in the background is left to backends from outside Django (`docs/topics/tasks.txt`).
`TASKS` maps aliases to backends; its default names `ImmediateBackend` under `"default"` (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

Its `TaskBackendHandler.create_connection` imports the class under `"BACKEND"` and makes it with the alias and the alias's dictionary; a failed import, and an alias `TASKS` lacks, raise `InvalidTaskBackend` (`django/tasks/__init__.py:TaskBackendHandler`).
`clear_tasks_handlers`, a receiver of `setting_changed`, empties the handler when `TASKS` changes (`django/tasks/signals.py:clear_tasks_handlers`).

Flags, all false in the base, say what a backend can do: `BaseTaskBackend.supports_defer`, `BaseTaskBackend.supports_async_task`, `BaseTaskBackend.supports_priority` and `BaseTaskBackend.supports_get_result`, the last for results read from any thread or process (`django/tasks/backends/base.py:BaseTaskBackend`).
The system check `check_tasks` runs each backend's `BaseTaskBackend.check` (`django/tasks/checks.py:check_tasks`).
`task` is used bare or with options (`django/tasks/base.py:task`).
Since 6.1 any other keyword argument goes to that class too, for a subclass that declares it (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

`Task` is a frozen dataclass with keyword-only fields: `Task.func`, `priority` (0), `backend` and `queue_name` (`"default"`), `run_after` (the earliest time to run) and `takes_context` (`django/tasks/base.py:Task`).

`Task.__post_init__` passes every new task to its backend's `BaseTaskBackend.validate_task`, so a task is checked when the decorator makes it, when `using` copies it and when it is unpickled; both built-in backends check it again in `enqueue` (`django/tasks/backends/base.py:BaseTaskBackend.validate_task`).
The function is a Python function whose qualified name holds no `"<locals>"` (`django/utils/inspect.py:is_module_level_function`).

`TaskResult.__post_init__` passes the arguments through `normalize_json`, which keeps strings, integers, floats, booleans and `None`, makes mappings dictionaries and other sequences lists, decodes bytes as UTF-8, and refuses anything else with `TypeError`, bytes that will not decode with `ValueError` (`django/utils/json.py:normalize_json`).
The documentation's reason: both are serialized to JSON (`docs/topics/tasks.txt`).

A `TaskResult` records one enqueueing: the task, a `TaskResult.id`, a `TaskResult.status`, the times it was enqueued, started, last attempted and finished, the arguments, the alias, `TaskResult.errors` and `TaskResult.worker_ids` (`django/tasks/base.py:TaskResult`).
`TaskResult.refresh` copies the status, times, errors, workers and return value of the backend's result (`django/tasks/base.py:TaskResult.refresh`).

`TaskError.exception_class` imports the class only when asked, splitting the path at its last dot, so a class nested in another, as `Model.DoesNotExist` is, is not found (`django/tasks/base.py:TaskError.exception_class`, `django/utils/module_loading.py:import_string`).

`ImmediateBackend.enqueue` validates the task, makes a `READY` result, runs it, and returns that same object (`django/tasks/backends/immediate.py:ImmediateBackend.enqueue`, `django/tasks/backends/immediate.py:ImmediateBackend._execute_task`):

An exception whose class is defined inside a function escapes instead, as the `ValueError` of `qualname`, which gives such a class no dotted path, and leaves the result `RUNNING` (`django/utils/module_loading.py:qualname`).

`django/tasks/signals.py` connects to each a receiver that logs to `"django.tasks"`: DEBUG on enqueueing, INFO on start and success, ERROR on failure with the exception, which `sys.exc_info` still holds because the signal is sent inside the handler, as the receiver's comment says (`django/tasks/signals.py:log_task_finished`).

`DummyBackend.enqueue` validates the task, makes a `READY` result, appends it to `DummyBackend.results`, sends `task_enqueued`, and returns a deep copy, "to prevent mutation issues", says the comment (`django/tasks/backends/dummy.py:DummyBackend.enqueue`).
Since 6.1 a `Task` pickles as its fields, the function replaced by `Task.module_path`, its dotted path (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.__reduce__`).
A `TaskResult` pickles with its task inside it (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
